entries.group: the L418 self-consistency guard: both disjuncts are held False by the construction above it on every reachable bundle, so weakening or->and is unobservable
entries.grounds: Mutant confirmed: L418 `if lacks != owed or len(candidate['approvals'])+len(withheld) != len(data['approvals'])` -> `... and ...`. This is migrate's defensive self-consistency guard (the comment at L413-414 states the invariant 'what the candidate lacks is exactly what was withheld -- never less or more'). or->and differs from the original ONLY when exactly one disjunct is True. On every bundle that REACHES L418 (shape-valid L372-374, kernel-loadable L375-381, every contract compiled L384-388, plan rebound L389-405) both disjuncts are False: (A) lacks != owed is False because unapproved(data)==[] (the idx-103 proof) makes owed = {exposed contract x its requirement_ids}, and the candidate drops exactly the withheld approvals (all approvals of exposed contracts + the non-binding ones), so unapproved(candidate)==owed; (B) the count is False because candidate keeps `[a for a in data['approvals'] if _key(a) not in dropped]` while withheld iterates the full approvals tuple, so each removal is counted -- measured by me: LedgerLock 53 kept + 6 withheld == 59, and migrate returns without raising. A single-disjunct-True state requires migrate's own construction to be internally inconsistent, which no valid, reachable bundle produces. Not provably EQUIVALENT (the two disjuncts guard independent failure modes and are not forced equal by one code fact), so AUDITED. The guard only chooses raise vs return; no reader depends on which. SURVIVED all 5 registered migrate kill files that exercise migrate (test_v21_kills3_A03, _T03a, _T03b, _migrate_semantics, _identity), measured by me in an isolated copy tree with PATH stripped of opencode; harness positive-controlled (mutants on fields the tests DO read -- idx116 'subject', idx117 'subject_absence', idx139 'contracts_to_approve', idx140 'loads' -- are KILLED by test_v21_migrate_semantics, so the SURVIVED results are real passes, not non-loading modules).

callers of migrate: main() L1071 (return -> write+print; MigrationError -> `refused:` exit 2), validation/v21/context_gap.py (uses migrate()[0] on trusted bundles); none feeds a bundle that makes exactly one disjunct True

entries.grounds: Mutant confirmed at snapshot: L402 `new_plan = Plan.create(id=..., baseline=..., obligations=tuple(obligations), ...)` -> `list(obligations)`. Plan.__post_init__ (aisef2/plan/obligation.py:89-102) does `obligations = tuple(self.obligations) if isinstance(self.obligations, (list, tuple)) else None` (:93), refuses an empty one (:94-95), and stores the tuple with object.__setattr__ (:96) BEFORE plan_hash is computed (:99-100). So a list argument is normalised to a tuple at construction, identically to a tuple argument; the stored obligations, the plan_hash, and every downstream read are therefore type-insensitive regardless of how new_plan is later used. At the placeholder the probe lists $5 only `if [ -e "$5" ]` (PROBE L71), and /nonexistent exists inside only as (a) bubblewrap's parent directory of a mount below it, where every listed entry is that mount's own first path component (shown <= names, L567-569, in both), or (b) a bind of a HOST directory /nonexistent with content (an operator read_only entry — wrap L185-187 refuses a missing one —, the client's directory, the workspace, a bare common git directory). (b) needs a real host directory of that name AND bound by the wrapper; nothing the wrapper builds creates it and by convention it does not exist. There the original admits and the mutant refuses with 'HOME shows more than...' though no HOME is set: a false refusal, fail-closed; neither admits a breach, and the listing at the placeholder is not the operator's HOME (wrap's HOME check at L190 reads expanduser separately; the probe never listed it).

The read is guarded by finding.is_file() at L297, so a regular file won't raise IsADirectoryError; OSError is effectively unreachable here (transient I/O only). Even if it fired, verify.verify's outer except Exception (verify.py:221) -> REFUTED, identical to the original (held=None -> problem 'the finding it observes is not at ...'). The ValueError ('{ not json') and AttributeError ('{"finding": "F"}' -> str.get) branches ARE exercised by test_the_finding_is_compared... and are KEPT by the mutant. Survives both kill files (unit 59 OK, run 25 OK).

entries.group: G-count-verdict
entries.grounds: mutant_view confirms `present = sum(1 for p in folder.glob('*.json') if p.is_file() and _NAME.fullmatch(p.name))` -> `... if p.is_file() or _NAME.fullmatch(p.name)`. The author's grounds claim a verify verdict flip (spurious REFUTED, or masked -> 'false VERIFIED'). DISPROVEN by direct reproduction against the snapshot: directory {S1.1.p1.json (valid), stray.json}: with written=1 ORIGINAL problems=['...stray.json is not a file this release writes'] (no count problem); MUTANT problems=[same, 'RUN.json states 1 written, the directory holds 2']. With written=2 ORIGINAL=[stray-problem, 'holds 1']; MUTANT=[stray-problem only]. In EVERY case the verdict is REFUTED either way, because the only file that makes `present` diverge (a stray real .json, or a _NAME-named non-file i.e. a directory) is INDEPENDENTLY a main-loop problem: a stray *.json -> 'is not a file this release writes' (L281-282) AND an evidence_manifest mismatch (run.py:429 globs *.json, so stray.json is in `fresh` but not `stored`); a _NAME-named directory -> read fails -> 'is not a probe observation' (L286-289). So the mutant never emits 'NO problem'/false VERIFIED. It only changes the presence/content of the operator-read count-mismatch MESSAGE, which no program parses and which is always accompanied by an independent true problem. The count check is also a redundant second defense for removal (the _run test says 'refuted by the manifest AND by the count'). By the audit's own dividing line (REFUTED only where the verify verdict can flip), this is AUDITED, not test-owed. Survives both kill files (unit 59 OK, run 25 OK).

For the reachable OSErrors on this read_text path (PermissionError/EACCES, IsADirectoryError/EISDIR), e.strerror is a truthy string, so `or` yields strerror ('Permission denied') while `and` yields `e` (str(e), which adds the errno and the RUN.json PATH). entries.grounds: CORRECTED GROUNDS. Mutant: holder = runs[0] if runs else {'unread': []} (drops 'unaccounted'). holder['unaccounted'] is read only inside unknown() (L720-722) via the final siblings loop L770-774 (listed/sibling_of errors on the fallback holder). The else-dict is used ONLY when `runs` is empty. The author's condition is INCOMPLETE: `runs` is empty iff (a) predecessor is None [then at=None, the L756 while is skipped], OR (b) child is not None AND key(child)==key(predecessor) [then key(predecessor) is pre-seeded in `seen`]. Neither occurs at any caller: run.py:524 calls lineage_account only inside `if predecessor is not None:` (L518) and passes out (a fresh run dir, != predecessor) -> rules out BOTH (a) and (b); verify.py:86 passes pathlib.Path(c['path']) (non-None) and out (!=) -> rules out both; bundle_cli.py:947 passes run_dir (non-None) with child=None -> seen=set(), the first while iteration adds, so runs is non-empty (the author's 'child=None so never empty' is only true because run_dir is non-None). run.py:518's `if predecessor is not None` guard -- the load-bearing fact that rules out case (a) -- was not cited by the author. So the else-branch is dead for every caller; when it is never reached the mutant has no effect; if it were reached AND a final listed()/sibling_of() hit a LineageRefused/unreadable claim, unknown() would KeyError on the missing 'unaccounted' key (a real behavioural difference -> not EQUIVALENT, correctly AUDITED). Measurement: PASS on x_lineage_proof, defects_verify, pw_lineage_unread, defects_lineage2, kills3_T09b, kills3_T09c, pw_lineage_spend (no test constructs runs-empty).

entries.group: T25-EQ-URLERROR-IS-OSERROR: a subclass listed next to its base class in one except tuple
entries.grounds: preflight.py:61 is ONE clause `except (urllib.error.URLError, OSError, ValueError, http.client.HTTPException, RecursionError) as e:`; except-tuple matching is isinstance matching and urllib/error.py:19 `class URLError(OSError)` (CPython 3.14.7; HTTPError :35 and ContentTooShortError :70 derive from URLError): every URLError the try block can raise is matched by element 1 (OSError) into the same handler with the same `e`, and the body reads type(e).__name__ (the instance's class, not the listed one). HTTPError is taken by the clause before (preflight.py:56) in both. Verified by me against the installed stdlib (class MROs printed: URLError, HTTPError, ContentTooShortError all have OSError in their MRO; HTTPException, IncompleteRead, RecursionError do not and are listed separately). kill_check of the behavioural scratch test (URLError and ContentTooShortError answered with their class name): [17] SURVIVED, as a proof by hierarchy requires.

entries.group: T28-EQ-ROLE-AT-CANDIDATE: the label reaches route() only and every CANDIDATE row is role-independent (own trace per mutant, own label)
entries.grounds: Re-derived at the snapshot (story_runner.py, proof.py, routing.py, outcome.py, format3.py, merge.py are byte-identical to c4c1720, i.e. to the proof's own base). Value flow: story_runner.py:247-248 builds `preserved` (ObligationRole is read at no other line of the module but :139 `o.role.value` from plan.obligations); :250 `spec_id, role = obligations.get(cid) or preserved[cid]` (the plan's own role wins whenever the cid is one of the story's obligations); :251-253 hands `role` to prove() with the literal point MeasurementPoint.CANDIDATE. In prove() (proof.py:80-111) `role` is read once, at :107 `route(bound, spec, point, role)`; prove() refuses PARENT first (:86-87); the Proof (:28-37), the probe/evaluated payloads (plain(record)), the proof/verified payload (format3.verified_payload :233-246) and the gate row (`proof:{cid}`, :255-256) carry no role, and the Party range name is built from `under = criterion/point` (:88, :69). In route/row_for (routing.py:96-130) role has three readers: the isinstance guard (:114-115; all three labels are ObligationRole members), the table lookup (:125-126) and the fail-closed text (:102-103). Every role-keyed row of _EXECUTED is at PARENT (:70, :73, :76); the CANDIDATE rows (:81-86) are keyed role None, so .get((C, sat, reason, label)) misses and the `or` falls to (C, sat, reason, None): the same Route for any label. The fail-closed text is reachable only when row_for returns None; at CANDIDATE it cannot, by totality: Executed.__post_init__ (outcome.py:43-50) allows a reason only on INDETERMINATE and only an IndeterminateReason, which has exactly PRECONDITION_ABSENT and NON_CONTROLLER_SIGNAL (:28-33); contract_satisfaction (:71-79) yields SATISFIED/UNSATISFIED (no reason) or INDETERMINATE; the table has (C,S,None), (C,U,None), (C,I,PA), (C,I,NCS); UNRUNNABLE/INVALID_SPEC return at routing.py:120-123 before the lookup. The only place INTRODUCE differs from PRESERVE in the table is the PARENT PRECONDITION_ABSENT row (:70 READY vs :73 PRECONDITION_BROKEN); PARENT is refused by prove() before any role is read, so that row is unreachable from this call site (story_admission.py:80, the PARENT caller, passes the plan's obligation.role).

entries.group: T28-EQ-ROLE-AT-CANDIDATE: the label reaches route() only and every CANDIDATE row is role-independent (own trace per mutant, own label)
entries.grounds: Re-derived from BASE c4c1720, not taken from the hand-over. Value flow: story_runner.py:247-248 builds `preserved` (`ObligationRole` is read at no other line of that module); :250 `spec_id, role = obligations.get(cid) or preserved[cid]` (the plan's own role wins whenever the cid is one of the story's obligations); :251-253 hands `role` to prove() with the literal point MeasurementPoint.CANDIDATE. In prove() (proof.py:80-111) `role` is read once, at :107 `route(bound, spec, point, role)`; prove() refuses PARENT first (:86-87), and the Proof (:28-37), the probe/evaluated payloads (plain(record), protocol.py:189-200), the proof/verified payload (format3.verified_payload :233-246) and the gate row (`proof:{cid}`) carry no role. In route/row_for (routing.py:96-127) role has three readers: the isinstance guard (:114-115; all three labels are ObligationRole members), the table lookup (:125-126) and the fail-closed text (:102-103). Lookup: every role-keyed row of _EXECUTED is at PARENT (:70, :73, :76); the CANDIDATE rows (:81-85) are keyed role None, so .get((C, sat, reason, label)) misses and the `or` falls to the (C, sat, reason, None) row: the same Route for any label. The text is reachable only when row_for returns None; at CANDIDATE it cannot, by totality: Executed.__post_init__ (outcome.py:43-49) allows a reason only on INDETERMINATE and only an IndeterminateReason, which has exactly PRECONDITION_ABSENT and NON_CONTROLLER_SIGNAL (:28-33); contract_satisfaction (:71-79) yields SATISFIED/UNSATISFIED (reason None) or INDETERMINATE; the table has (C,S,None), (C,U,None), (C,I,PA), (C,I,NCS); UNRUNNABLE/INVALID_SPEC return at routing.py:120-123 before the lookup. Experiment (review/probe_attempt_label_identity.py, corroboration not proof): the real run_story/_attempt/GitWorkspace/two-party proof over three results of the affected PRESERVE criterion at the candidate (UNSATISFIED, SATISFIED, subject ABSENT -> SUBJECT_ABSENT_AT_CANDIDATE), label PRESERVE vs the mutant's label (ObligationRole is substituted in story_runner, which is the mutant exactly): the spy sees the label differ, the whole journal (types and payloads, SHAs/digests normalised by first appearance; BASE-vs-BASE control identical) and the attempt outcomes are identical in all 6 comparisons. Also re-ran the hand-over's routing probe: 56 cells, one Route across the 3 roles. [145] label VERIFY: VERIFY and PRESERVE have identical rows at every point (routing.py:73 and :76 differ only in the `rule` prose), and VERIFY is a role this call site already hands to prove() at the candidate: continuation.verify_at_candidate is every admission obligation of the story, any role (drift.py:89-90), each proved with the plan role from obligations_of. entries.group: campaign 9 survivor audit
entries.grounds: Confirmed: conclude() (cli_invocation.py:904) `said.acquire(blocking=False)`->`blocking=True`. said = threading.Lock() (883), acquired non-blocking in settle(901) and conclude(904) and NEVER released (no said.release in the HARNESS, grep). conclude is reached ONLY from the daemon Timer built in deadline()(908, timer.daemon=True, never joined/cancelled). When the lock is FREE (deadline wins the race) both acquire at once and write RESULT(deadline)/END identically; when HELD (the subject already settled) the non-blocking call returns False and writes nothing, the blocking call parks forever and also writes nothing -- the acquire is atomic either way, so the RESULT winner, protocol file and exit status are identical. The only difference is a parked daemon thread, which is not a range member and is not read by the parent (_watch reads the protocol file and the range's wait status); interpreter shutdown abandons daemon threads. EQUIVALENT by code (author's park.py measurement corroborates equal exit time). Campaign measured SURVIVED.

exceptions_checked: (campaign 9)

entries.group: campaign 9 survivor audit
entries.grounds: Confirmed: inside() (cli_invocation.py:948) `[spec.origin] if spec.origin and spec.has_location else ...` with the `and` operands swapped to `spec.has_location and spec.origin`. The expression's value is used ONLY as the truth condition of a conditional-expression, and bool(A and B) == bool(B and A) for all A,B (AND truth value is commutative), so the SAME branch is taken in every case regardless of spec type. spec.origin (plain attr) and spec.has_location (ModuleSpec property returning self._set_fileattr, a bool) are side-effect-free, so swapping evaluation order cannot raise or differ. EQUIVALENT by code (simpler and more general than the author's PathFinder enumeration, which is sound corroboration). Not separately measured (pure boolean-commutativity proof); the campaign measured SURVIVED.

entries.group: G-SEARCH-STOPPED-UNREAD: _SEARCH_STOPPED's ObservationKind is never read. It is passed once, at cli_invocation.py:351 `_after_dispatch(run, _SEARCH_STOPPED)` with the return value DISCARDED. _after_dispatch (python_callable.py:379-389) returns its `observation` argument unchanged when run.ledger has no stages (discarded at the unassigned call site) and otherwise raises ProbeInterrupted built only from the ledger stages, never referencing the argument. entries.group: G-SAID-DEFENSIVE-GUARD: _said (cli_invocation.py:382-388) is a defensive reader of the worker's output file, called only at 356/369/374 inside search_in_worker as '<message>' + _said(log); log is always the regex worker's own worker.log, created locally at 335 and read right after the worker ends. The sole writer of that file is the process launched at 339 running the FIXED REGEX_WORKER, whose imports are pinned to {json,re,sys} (test_v21_r5_regex_worker.py:419-420): it writes b'0'/b'1' to the RESULT file, and on a crash only a UTF-8 (ASCII) traceback to its stderr->log; it never removes the log and never writes invalid UTF-8. entries.grounds: The OSError branch of _said returns ''->None. _said is consumed only as '<message>'+_said(log) (356/369/374), so None would raise TypeError and break search_in_worker -- but the branch fires only if pathlib.Path(log).read_bytes() raises OSError, i.e. the just-created local worker.log (open 'wb' at 335) is unreadable when read right after the worker ends. REGEX_WORKER is fixed kernel code (launched 339) that never removes/chmods the log; every FailureModes stand-in leaves a readable log. The branch is dead on every real/tested path, so ''/None is unobservable. Not EQUIVALENT (a real FS fault WOULD make None observable), but no named consumer/test reaches it -> AUDITED.
